{"cc":[{"text":"Patient returns for joint injection.","start_char":54,"end_char":89}],"hpi":[{"text":"56-year-old male with osteoarthritis of the right great toe MTP joint
returns for follow-up corticosteroid injection. He had a similar
injection three months ago with good relief lasting approximately ten
weeks. Pain has now returned and is interfering with his daily walks.
No new symptoms.","start_char":113,"end_char":331}],"exam_findings":[{"text":"Right first MTP joint: tenderness on palpation, mild crepitus with
range of motion, no warmth, no effusion, no overlying skin changes.
Range of motion 25 degrees dorsiflexion, 10 degrees plantarflexion,
mild pain at end-range dorsiflexion.","start_char":345,"end_char":515}],"mdm":[{"text":"Right first MTP osteoarthritis with recurrent symptoms responsive to
prior corticosteroid injection. Discussed risks and benefits of
injection including infection, post-injection flare, fat pad atrophy,
and the limitations of repeat steroid use. Patient consents to repeat
injection.","start_char":529,"end_char":742}],"procedure_note":[{"text":"Following informed consent: right first MTP joint prepped with
chlorhexidine. 1 mL of triamcinolone 40 mg/mL mixed with 1 mL of 1%
lidocaine injected intra-articularly using sterile technique. Patient
tolerated well. No bleeding or complications.","start_char":754,"end_char":944}],"ambiguous_segments":[]}
